response.justification: Strong, versatile senior engineer with 15+ years of broad experience, but the profile is fundamentally misaligned with the core requirement of 8 years of C++ programming — the resume shows roughly 7 months of C/C++ work at National Instruments plus an academic project, with the bulk of the career in TypeScript/Node.js, D, and web/full-stack development. Distributed-systems exposure exists (low-latency microservices at Sociomantic handling millions of requests/sec, Kubernetes deployment of GISCollective), but there is no evidence of large-scale cloud compute platform ownership, production cloud architecture at scale, or a formal technical leadership role mentoring cloud/DevOps engineers. Mentoring credentials via workshops and community teaching are a genuine positive, yet not enough to offset the C++ and infrastructure-scale gaps for a technical lead on an internal compute platform.
strengths: Deep, varied 15+ year engineering background across web, mobile, embedded, and systems
Proven low-latency distributed systems work at Sociomantic (millions of req/sec)
Strong mentoring/teaching track record: workshops, courses, conference talks, OSS tooling
concerns: Far short of 8 years C++; only ~7 months of professional C/C++ work
No production cloud compute platform architecture or large-scale infra ownership
No formal technical leadership role managing priorities, timelines, or cloud/DevOps engineers

key_factors.factor: Lack of cloud/compute platform leadership experience
